text:
lyla: noticing increased 502s for internal inference in ap-south-1 and eu-west-2 starting ~08:17 UTC. Symptoms differ: session ticket unwrap fails and cert rotation attempts produce partial chains.

omar: can you paste small logs?

lyla: proxy extract:
```
2026-06-20T08:18:03Z proxy[edge-aps]: tls: session ticket unwrap failed: KMS AccessDenied for key arn:aws:kms:ap-south-1:...:alias/redwood-session-hsm (principal=svc-session-agent)
2026-06-20T08:18:06Z proxy[edge-euw]: cert-rotator: published cert with missing intermediate; ocsp responder rejected: 403
```

fred: audit shows a key policy edit on our HSM-backed alias plus an RBAC roll that removed an IAM role mapping used by the rotator and session agents. The policy-shipper run changed PutRolePolicy -> ENFORCING and a separate key policy edit tightened kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt to a tag condition.

policy-shipper: audit: PutRolePolicy role=keystore-hsm-prod user=infra-ci change=chg-8891 mode=ENFORCING

kms-bot: KMS Audit: AccessDenied | RequestId=r-4a9b | Principal=svc-cert-rotator | Action=Decrypt | Key=alias/redwood-session-hsm | Reason=principal missing in keypolicy

omar: So two layers: the HSM keypolicy rejects principals not explicitly in the key ACL; the RBAC rollout removed tags causing the principal to be excluded. The rotator could publish an incomplete chain because it couldn't decrypt the intermediate signing key after rotation.

lyla: Impact: internal generate endpoints 5xx up ~10% in ap-south-1 and ~7% in eu-west-2. Customer-facing endpoints still ok for now but we should act fast.

fred: immediate mitigations I suggest: (A) add the rotator and session-agent principals back to the key policy (B) create a scoped short-lived HSM grant (via automation) allowing Decrypt/GenerateDataKey for the specific principals for 30m (C) revert the RBAC PutRolePolicy to SHADOW in affected regions.

policy-shipper: run:revert -> starting revert to SHADOW for role keystore-hsm-prod (id=deploy-9941)

sre_rotations: opening INC-2026-2107 and paging owners. I'll add a routing rule to move new sessions to nodes backed by the older session-key alias while we repair.

omar: Can we avoid full keypolicy edits during policy rollouts? Key policies on HSM keys are more sensitive. Propose an automation: when a PutRolePolicy touches keystore roles, policy-shipper must trigger a keypolicy-impact check that runs a dry-run decrypt/generate using target principals in the region. If any keypolicy denies, block ENFORCING until manual approval.

fred: Also: we should have a fallback: session-ticket encryption should prefer a dedicated regional session alias (non-HSM) with automated grants from the HSM rotator. That way HSM keypolicy changes don't instantly break session unwrap across all regions.

lyla: For immediate observability: make proxy emit structured audit events on unwrap failures including kms_request_id, key_alias, principal and keypolicy_response. Eg: '{"event":"session_unwrap_fail","region":"ap-south-1","kms_request_id":"r-4a9b","key":"alias/redwood-session-hsm","principal":"svc-session-agent","reason":"KeyPolicy:NotPrincipal"}'. That will help correlate keypolicy edits with outages.

policy-shipper: note: adding guardrail - any PutRolePolicy touching keystore-* will now require a KeyPolicyDryRun check and sec approval to proceed to ENFORCING (PR opened by @omar).

kms-bot: temporary grant created (id=g-pp33) for principal=svc-cert-rotator,svc-session-agent actions=[Decrypt,GenerateDataKey] key=alias/redwood-session-hsm TTL=00:30:00

lyla: after the grant, unwrap failures dropped in ap-south within 90s and cert rotations completed with full chains in eu-west within 3m.

sre_rotations: routing change applied; traffic normalized regionally. Keeping incident open for follow-ups.

omar: follow-ups: 1) implement KeyPolicyDryRun in policy-shipper CI (owner=policy-shipper) 2) emit structured session_unwrap_fail events from proxy + dashboard alert for kms keypolicy denies (owner=observability/lyla) 3) design regional session-key aliases with automated grant flow (owner=fred) 4) update cert-rotator to abort rotation if it detects partial chain and to retry only after verification (owner=rotator) 5) add a runbook entry: 'HSM keypolicy or RBAC change -> KMS denies -> mTLS unwrap/rotation failures' with checklist for emergency grants and routing.

fred: security note: automated short-lived grants need an approval trail and auditable justification; we'll wire this into the incident system so grants created during incidents are logged and require postmortem review.

lyla: agree. I'll draft the postmortem and include the keypolicy dry-run automation and metric additions. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
